Definition: feminine from G1722 and the base of G1476; an ambuscade, i.e. (figuratively) murderous purpose:--lay wait. See also G1749.
BiblicalUsage: An ambush — a lying in wait to kill. Paul's nephew heard of the Jews lying in wait for Paul in Acts 23:16 and told him, and the chief priests asked Festus to send Paul to Jerusalem, laying wait in the way to kill him, in Acts 25:3.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the ambush failed because God had a nephew listening at the right moment, and no plot against His servant goes forward without His leave.
